response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-18
CLINICAL INDICATION: Surveillance. History of treated colon adenocarcinoma. Assess for new pulmonary nodules.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. A. Rahimi (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-05-14
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same view as prior. Image processing and display contrast differ slightly between the films, and the current image has a wider border. A belt and buckle overlie the upper abdomen on the prior only.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1, left hilum, nodule or mass: small dense rounded opacity at the lateral margin of the left hilum. Not time-sensitive. Stable and similar in size compared with prior. Both reads agreed.
- F4, right hilum, nodule or mass: small rounded dense focus over the right hilum. Not time-sensitive. Similar to prior. INDETERMINATE: the reads disagreed (only one of two reads reported it). May be a vessel end-on or a small calcified node.
- F2, right hilum, other: small dense focus over the right hilum. Not time-sensitive. Similar to prior. INDETERMINATE: the reads disagreed (only one of two reads reported it). F2 and F4 appear to describe the same focus. May be a small calcified node or a vessel end-on.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi unremarkable. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, collapse or interstitial pattern. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. Small, dense, well-defined rounded opacity at the lateral margin of the left hilum (F1), present in the same position on the prior with similar shape, density and apparent size. No new lung opacity in any zone.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortic knuckle and aortopulmonary window preserved. Hila normal in size and position, with no interval hilar enlargement. Small dense focus at the right hilum (F4, F2; indeterminate, reads disagreed) and small dense rounded opacity at the left hilum (F1). Both are unchanged from prior.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles sharp. No pleural thickening. No effusion or pneumothorax on either study.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly prominent on a PA film, with a rounded left ventricular contour (F3). Heart borders sharp. Same size and shape as prior. Cardiothoracic ratio not measured; radiologist to measure in PACS.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture and no destructive bone lesion seen in the ribs, clavicles, shoulders or visible spine. Bilateral breast shadows overlie the lower zones. No soft tissue gas. No lines, tubes, ports, pacemaker or surgical clips. External objects only.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: None. No new pulmonary nodule is seen on the current film compared with the prior. Differences in image processing and display contrast limit judgment of a subtle density change in the small hilar opacities.
- Unchanged: Left hilar dense rounded opacity (F1), right hilar dense focus (F4/F2), cardiac silhouette (F3), mediastinal contour, pleural spaces and lungs. Sizes are described in words only (similar); no measurements were provided.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense left hilar opacity a calcified granuloma or node, or a non-calcified nodule? | Reason: The opacity is small, and a frontal film at this resolution cannot confirm calcification or show its margins in detail. It could also be a vessel end-on. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS and any older films. CT chest if calcification or long-term stability cannot be confirmed.
- Is the small dense right hilar focus a calcified node or a vessel end-on? | Reason: On a single frontal projection, a small hilar density cannot be separated from a normal vessel seen end-on. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest if clinically relevant.
- Is there a retrocardiac or retrosternal abnormality? | Reason: Only frontal films were provided. The area behind the heart is seen through the cardiac shadow only. | Recommend: Lateral view if there is clinical concern.
- Is the left perihilar nodule calcified, which would be consistent with a granuloma? | Reason: The nodule is small and these are downsampled frontal radiographs. Density and internal calcification cannot be confirmed at this resolution. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS and compare with any older studies to establish long-term stability. CT chest if calcification or stability cannot be confirmed.
- Is the small dense focus over the right hilum a vessel end-on, a calcified node or a small nodule? | Reason: It is a small density superimposed on hilar vessels on a frontal view alone, and the image resolution is limited. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with a lateral view if available. CT chest if it remains unexplained.
- Does the prominent left heart border reflect enlargement of a specific chamber or of the pulmonary artery? | Reason: A frontal radiograph shows the contour only. It cannot separate the left atrial appendage, the pulmonary artery segment and normal variation. | Recommend: Lateral chest view and clinical correlation. Echocardiography if clinically indicated.
- Is there a retrocardiac or hidden lower lobe abnormality? | Reason: Only frontal views are provided, and the retrocardiac region is partly obscured by the prominent cardiac silhouette. | Recommend: Lateral view.

IMPRESSION:
1. Small dense well-defined rounded opacity at the left hilum (F1), unchanged from prior with similar size, density and position. Calcified granuloma or node versus non-calcified nodule cannot be determined on this study (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
2. Small dense rounded focus over the right hilum (F4), similar to prior. Indeterminate; the reads disagreed. May be a vessel end-on or a small calcified node.
3. Small dense focus over the right hilum (F2), similar to prior. Indeterminate; the reads disagreed. Appears to describe the same focus as F4.
4. No new pulmonary nodule is seen on the current PA film compared with the prior. Frontal views alone cannot exclude small or retrocardiac nodules.
5. Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly prominent, unchanged from prior (F3, outside the indication).

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source images in PACS and any older films for the left and right hilar densities. CT chest if calcification or long-term stability cannot be confirmed. Interval not specified in the findings; attending to determine.
- Lateral chest view if there is clinical concern for retrocardiac or retrosternal abnormality or for the cardiac contour. Echocardiography if clinically indicated.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
